newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon to issue $400 million eurobond next year.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon to issue $400 million eurobond next year.

text.p: Lebanon will issue a $400 million eurobond in October 1997 to cover its three-year $400-million bond that matures that month, central bank deputy chief Nasser Saidi was quoted on Monday as saying.
"In October 1997, the first eurobond, for $400 million, will mature. It is natural that there will be a new issue to cover the principal of the due debt," Saidi told an-Nahar daily in an interview.
The government will need parliamentary approval for new eurobond issues.
Lebanon's first $400 million eurobond of September 1994 matures on October 14, 1997.
The government also issued in May a $100 million addition to a $300-million 9.125 percent bond issued in July 1995.
Last month, Information Minister Farid Makari said the finance ministry was preparing a $100 million eurobond for the state-run electricity utility.
"So long as we enjoy credibility in our monetary and financial reputation we will not find any difficulty in servicing the debts, neither today nor in future," Saidi said.
